verdict: Both mechanisms have source support. They expose different test-design gaps; no subject candidate or runtime outcome was generated or read.

hypotheses.name: Partial values omit schema defaults in projected get
hypotheses.source_conclusion: The public type allows Partial records. Original ordinary trait tests require omitted defaults to remain. Entity.get routes to deferredGet, which returns pending params directly. For an initially absent ordinary trait, flush applyDiff calls addTrait, which merges schema defaults.
hypotheses.test_design_gap: The existing deferred tests already observe get before and after flush, but their one-field schemas receive complete values. These inputs do not distinguish pending params from the full materialized record. A stronger observer alone cannot expose that omission.
required_conditions: Ordinary SoA trait with a legal partial record and initially absent trait.
Use constant defaults, or establish that default factories are pure, deterministic and stable across the two observations. Do not assume equal fresh factory objects by identity.
Use value snapshots or a stable primitive field. SoA public snapshot semantics do not make an AoS mutable alias equivalent.
Any changed input requires rechecking all retained expectations. In particular, the old expected explicit value cannot survive its omission without a new contract basis.

hypotheses.name: Projection omits effects from commands on related entities
hypotheses.source_conclusion: The queried entity projection skips commands for other entities. The flush path builds a relation graph over projected and live entities, then cascades destruction according to source/target direction. The original cascade tests already supply the cross-entity relation and destroy stimulus.
hypotheses.test_design_gap: The existing cascade tests observe only world.has after flush. They omit a before-flush observation through the explicitly contracted Entity.has/get. This is an observer/binding gap, not necessarily a weak-input gap.
required_conditions: Resolve relation direction and entity identity from the actual declaration and calls. Equal variable names do not prove binding.
The observer may target an entity affected by a command on another entity. Requiring the same command receiver would omit this family.
Only Entity.has/get are explicitly covered by the issue equivalence sentence. Do not automatically include world.has, isAlive or targetsFor.
Require a well-defined observer before and after flush, no unrelated intervening mutation, and full-test contract support. Dead-entity behavior or callback effects require separate justification.

general_abstraction: A phase-equivalence contract requires both a legal distinguishing state and an observer bound to the contract subject and its dependencies. Source tests may already provide either half. An algorithm should diagnose which half is missing before adding another generic phase check.
novelty_boundary: These are source diagnoses, not a new universal algorithm or proof of detection. Cross-task and unseen-task evidence is still required.
